root.name: Sicilian Defense: Myers Attack, with a4

overview: White plays the strange 2.a4 (or 2.h4) against the Sicilian, losing a tempo. Black develops with ...Nc6, ...d6 and ...Nf6 or even grabs the centre with ...d5. White hopes for a quiet game with a4 helping against ...b5, but he has not really developed. It is a surprise weapon.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Nf3, d4 and treat a4 as a restraint on ...b5
Hope Black overreaches against the rook-pawn advance

black_ideas.idea: Develop normally and take space with ...d5 or ...Nf6
Use the half-open c-file and lead in development

typical_structures.structure: Sicilian pawn asymmetry with a4 pawn
Open Sicilian structures after Nf3 and d4

character.notes: A slow, odd line where White has lost a tempo.

soundness.notes: Playable if pointless; Black is comfortably equal.

structure.notes: Sicilian asymmetry: half-open c-file for Black.

approach.notes: Rarely chosen by strong players; chosen for surprise.

level.notes: Nothing to study; not a good repertoire choice.
